videos.title: EARNINGS PANEL: AMZN, INTC, SNDK, RDDT, COIN, SBUX

findings.summary: A Schwab Network earnings panel walks through after-hours and just-released results for Amazon, Intel, SanDisk, Reddit, Coinbase, and Starbucks. Amazon and Intel are the big movers: Amazon missed on EPS and revenue (though AWS was roughly in line and guidance matched consensus) and fell about 5-11% in the discussion; Intel beat on EPS but missed on revenue and especially on next-quarter guidance, with shares down roughly 17-22%. SanDisk beat on all metrics and guided above estimates but slipped; Reddit beat on revenue and profit but warned of falling search referral traffic and weak guidance, and was down about 7-10%; Coinbase and Starbucks had mixed reports with moves of about 1% or less. The panelists largely attribute moves to guidance, cash flow concerns, AI spending, and AI search disruption, with speculation about how the calls will go.
macro_points: Panelists say negative free cash flow across most Mag Seven names outside Microsoft is starting to weigh on stocks, tied to heavy AI capex.
Intel says the PC slowdown will continue at least through the first half of 2027.
Panelists describe a broader negative tech tone and a weak earnings season, with the Nasdaq down about 1.5% on the day.
AI agents and personalized bots are seen as a long-term threat to search referral traffic and retail search businesses.
red_flags: Reaction-driven commentary: several moves are attributed to sentiment and a negative news cycle without much hard evidence.
Speculation that Intel may announce a new customer on the call to reverse the selloff, with no basis given.
Reddit warned daily active users could fall by a low double-digit percent if search referral declines continue.
Amazon free cash flow is negative on a trailing 12-month basis, with capex around 220 billion dollars.
Intel guidance missed consensus across revenue, EPS, and gross margin, and the host calls it a bad quarter.
Panelist speculates about a Starbucks and Chipotle tie-up, which the company had previously denied and was not in the report.

tickers.thesis: Panelists see Amazon's EPS and revenue misses as a concern, especially North America retail sales that they read as a consumer signal and a possible threat from AI shopping bots. AWS was roughly in line, and the next-quarter sales guide was near consensus. Negative free cash flow tied to AI capex is also raised as a worry, though the operating margin hit a record.

Panelists say Intel beat on EPS and data center/AI revenue, but missed on client computing revenue and on nearly every next-quarter guidance metric. They say the PC slowdown will last into 2027 and that fab issues in Israel explain only part of the guidance miss, so the stock is down sharply.

SanDisk beat on revenue, EPS, and gross margin and guided above consensus, plus announced a buyback and an 8-for-1 forward split. Panelists think the stock's small decline reflects a broader tech selloff and that the strong numbers may have been partly priced in.
tickers.catalyst: Fiscal Q1 2027 earnings and 8-for-1 split effective November 19

tickers.thesis: Reddit beat on revenue, net income, and adjusted EBITDA, but daily active users missed slightly and Q4 revenue and EBITDA guidance came in below estimates. Management flagged that falling search referral traffic could push DAUs down by a low double-digit percent, and panelists see the AI-search cannibalization risk as a major issue.

Coinbase beat on transaction and subscription revenue and adjusted EBITDA and gained crypto market share, though trading volume is slowing. The panelist sees prediction markets as a possible growth driver but questions competition from brokerages and the wide Q4 subscription guide.

Starbucks beat on EPS, operating margin, and U.S. comparable sales, and its fiscal 2027 EPS guide was slightly above consensus. Revenue fell 4% and international comps missed, which panelists see as a mixed report, with the U.S. turnaround continuing.
tickers.catalyst: Q4 fiscal 2026 earnings and fiscal 2027 guidance

The state's balance sheet reportedly holds about $75 billion more than in 2019, according to Rauch.
Prediction markets reportedly give the measure about a 25-30% chance of passing, per Rauch.
Billionaires reportedly spent over $300 million opposing the measure, per Zucman.
Some billionaires, including Larry Page and Peter Thiel, have reportedly moved or claimed to move out of California, which Rauch disputes as a practical matter.
red_flags: Claims of mass billionaire departures are contested; the panel disagrees on whether these moves are real.
Figures on illegal immigrant coverage costs, Medi-Cal growth, and billionaire tax payments are stated without sources and are disputed between panelists.

Panel discussion includes heated personal exchanges and some unsupported assertions (e.g., France comparisons) that were not verified.
